details:
Q1: Where should the allowlist of paths the review-blocked fix may commit come from?
Choices:
A) Only the files the blocked PR already changed, read from GitHub's paginated `pulls/<n>/files` list. The model has no say in it, but a fix that needs a new test or `changelog.d/` file would be refused.
B) The PR's changed files from GitHub, plus files the judge cites in `fix_description` / `remaining_issues[].file`. Judge-cited files are kept only if they pass the existing path checks (no globs, no `.git`, no traversal) and are not protected paths (see Q2). (RECOMMENDED)
C) Only the files the judge cites. **Note:** this is not provenance-verified, because the judge is the component the exploit targets.
Q2: How should protected paths (`.github/workflows/`, `.github/actions/`, `.github/ai/`, `scripts/`, `prompts/`, `.claude/`) be handled when `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=true`?
Choices:
A) A protected path may be committed only if the blocked PR itself already changed that exact path. Otherwise it is rejected, whatever `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS` says. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Always reject protected paths in this fix path. **Note:** this blocks most legitimate review-blocked fixes in coding-workflows, where PRs routinely change `scripts/`.
C) Keep today's behaviour for protected paths (allowed when `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=true`) and enforce only the Q1 allowlist.
Q3: What should happen when staged changes fall outside the allowlist?
Choices:
A) Reject the whole fix: no commit, no push, clean up the workspace. Log a new stable prefix (for example `REVIEW_BLOCKED_FIX_SCOPE_REJECTED`) listing the offending paths, send a Telegram WARNING, and count the attempt against `MAX_REVIEW_BLOCKED_RETRIES` so the existing retry/terminal ladder still moves forward. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Drop the out-of-scope paths and commit the rest.
C) Reject the fix and set `ai:needs-human` straight away.
Q4: Should the same guard also cover the standalone judge's fix commit path in `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh`?
Choices:
A) No. Fix only the poller path the finding cites (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`) and add contract tests in `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Yes. Put the check in a shared helper and use it from both the poller and `review_rb_judge.sh`.
